"Let $\Gamma$ be a graph with axial function $\alpha$. For each vertex $p$, let $\sigma_p$ be its index, let $F_p$ be the set of vertices that can be joined to $p$ by an ascending path, and let $E_p^-$ be the set of descending edges in $E_p$. Let $H(\Gamma,\alpha)$ be the equivariant cohomology ring and let $\mathbb S({\mathfrak g}^*)$ be the polynomial ring of constant maps. **Thom-class conjecture.** $H(\Gamma,\alpha)$ is freely generated as an $\mathbb S({\mathfrak g}^*)$-module by a family of Thom classes

$$
\tau_p^+\in H^k(\Gamma,\alpha),\qquad k=\sigma_p,
$$

 satisfying

$$
{\,}{support}\tau_p^+\subseteq F_p
$$

and

$$
\tau_p^+(p)=\prod_{e\in E_p^-}\alpha_e\quad(=:\nu_p^+).
$$

This gives a more explicit Morse-theoretic prediction than freeness alone, specifying generators, their degrees, supports, and values at their associated vertices; the supplied text gives no resolution status."

"Let $G$ and $G'$ be the symmetry groups specified in the claim, and write $M_G(a,b,c)_{-1}$ and $A_G(a,b,c)_{-1}$ for the corresponding matrices specialized at $q=-1$. Let $\operatorname{Sm}(N)$ denote the Smith normal form of $N$. **$q=-1$ cokernel conjecture.** The following relations should hold:

$$
\operatorname{Sm}(A_{G'}(a,b,c))=\operatorname{Sm}(M_G(a,b,c)_{-1})^2
$$

when $G=\langle1\rangle$ or $\langle\rho\rangle$ and $G'=\langle G,\kappa\rangle$;

$$
\operatorname{coker} A_G(a,b,c)_{-1}\cong\operatorname{coker} M_{G'}(a,b,c)^{\oplus2}
$$

when $G=\langle\tau\rangle$ or $\langle\rho,\tau\rangle$ and $G'=\langle\kappa\tau\rangle$ or $\langle\rho,\kappa\tau\rangle$, respectively; and

$$
\operatorname{coker} A_{G'}(a,b,c)\cong\operatorname{coker} A'_G(a,b,c)_{-1}
$$

when $G=\langle\tau\rangle$ or $\langle\rho,\tau\rangle$ and $G'=\langle G,\kappa\rangle$. This conjecture proposes a cokernel and Smith-form extension of Stembridge's $q=-1$ phenomenon for symmetry classes of plane partitions. The source presents it as conjectural and gives no proof or resolution, so it remains open."

"Let ${\cal P}_n^k$ denote the set of partitions of $[n]$ into $k$ blocks, and let $\mathop{\rm mak}$, $\mathop{\rm lmak}$, $\mathop{\rm mak}{}'$ and ${\mathop{\rm lmak}}'$ be the four partition statistics considered in the paper. Let $S_q(n,k)$ denote the classical q-Stirling number of the second kind. **Steingrímsson's conjecture.** The four statistics have generating function $S_q(n,k)$ on ${\cal P}_n^k$; equivalently,

$$
\sum_{\pi\in {\cal P}_n^k}q^{\mathop{\rm mak}(\pi)}=\sum_{\pi\in {\cal P}_n^k}q^{\mathop{\rm mak}{}'(\pi)}=\sum_{\pi\in {\cal P}_n^k}q^{{\mathop{\rm lmak}}'(\pi)}=\sum_{\pi\in {\cal P}_n^k}q^{\mathop{\rm lmak}(\pi)}=S_q(n,k).
$$

The conjecture concerns q-analogues of Stirling-number generating functions for set partitions; the supplied text identifies it as Steingrímsson's conjecture but gives no resolution status."

"Let ${\cal OP}_n^k$ be the set of ordered $k$-partitions of $[n]$, and let $\mathop{\rm bmaj}$ and $\mathop{\rm binv}$ be the block-major index and block-inversion statistics. Let $\mathop{\rm mak}$, $\mathop{\rm mak}{}'$, $\mathop{\rm lmak}{}'$ and $\mathop{\rm lmak}$ be the four statistics from the preceding definition. A statistic on ${\cal OP}_n^k$ is Euler–Mahonian when its generating function is $[k]_q!S_q(n,k)$. **Steingrímsson's conjecture.** Each of the following eight statistics is Euler–Mahonian:

$$
\mathop{\rm mak}+\mathop{\rm bmaj},\quad \mathop{\rm mak}{}'+\mathop{\rm bmaj},\quad \mathop{\rm lmak}{}'+\mathop{\rm bmaj},\quad \mathop{\rm lmak}+\mathop{\rm bmaj},
$$

$$
\mathop{\rm mak}+\mathop{\rm binv},\quad \mathop{\rm mak}{}'+\mathop{\rm binv},\quad \mathop{\rm lmak}{}'+\mathop{\rm binv},\quad \mathop{\rm lmak}+\mathop{\rm binv}.
$$

The claim proposes Euler–Mahonian extensions of q-Stirling statistics to ordered set partitions; the supplied text gives no evidence that it has been proved or disproved."

"Let $OMCUT_n$ be the cone of oriented multicuts, and let $G_{OMCUT_n}$ be its skeleton graph. For an oriented partition $A$, write $A^T$ for its reversal, and write $A<B$ when $A$ is a proper refinement of $B$; write $A\mathrel{\dot{<}}B$ when every part of $A$ is a proper subset of a part of $B$. Let $p'(n)$ denote the number of oriented-multicut extreme rays.

**Oriented-multicut adjacency conjecture.** (i) An oriented multicut $\delta'(A)$ is not adjacent to every oriented multicut $\delta'(B)$ such that $B<A^T$. (ii) The orbit represented by the oriented cut $\delta'(\{1\},\{2,\dots,n\})$ is the unique orbit whose extreme rays are not adjacent only to the oriented multicuts described in (i); its total adjacency is $p'(n)-p'(n-1)-1$, and this is maximal. (iii) An extreme ray in the orbit represented by $\delta'(\{1,2\},\{3,\dots,n\})$ is not adjacent only to oriented multicuts $\delta'(B)$ for which either $B<(\{1,2\},\{3,\dots,n\})^T$, or $B$ is a cyclic shift of some $C$ with $C\mathrel{\dot{<}}(\{1,2\},\{3,\dots,n\})$. (iv) The diameter of $G_{OMCUT_n}$ is $2$.

The source gives these as conjectural adjacency properties; no general verification or resolution is supplied in the provided text."

"Let $\lambda$, $\mu$, and $\tilde\mu$ be number partitions. For number partitions $\lambda>\mu$, the inclusion $i(\mu,\lambda):\delta_\mu\rightarrow\delta_\lambda$ induces a homomorphism

$$
i(\mu,\lambda)_*:\widetilde H_*(\delta_{\,\operatorname{Res}\,\mu})\rightarrow\widetilde H_*(\delta_{\,\operatorname{Res}\,\lambda}).
$$
 **Noncanonicity conjecture.** There exist number partitions $\lambda$, $\mu$, and $\tilde\mu$ such that $\lambda>\mu$, $\lambda>\tilde\mu$, $\operatorname{Res}\,\mu=\operatorname{Res}\,\tilde\mu$, and the homomorphisms $i(\mu,\lambda)_*$ and $i(\tilde\mu,\lambda)_*$ induced by the respective inclusion maps are nonisomorphic. The conjecture asserts that the induced map depends on more than the resonance sets of its source and target, so no unique map $i(\operatorname{Res}\,\mu,\operatorname{Res}\,\lambda)_*$ can be defined."

The known inclusions are ${\cal C}_1\subseteq{\cal C}_2\subseteq{\cal C}_3\subseteq{\cal C}_4$.

$$
{\cal C}_2\neq{\cal C}_3.
$$

"Write $p$ repeated opening parentheses as $(^p$ and $p$ repeated opening parentheses followed by $p$ closing parentheses as $(\ldots)_p=(^p\ldots)^p$. For matchings of the form $(_s_t)_p$, write $[s,t,p]$. Let $a_F$ be the coefficient of matching $F$ in the stationary state of $H^{\rm C}_{2p+2s+2t}$. **Ciucu–Krattenthaler stationary-state coefficient conjecture.** For $F=[s,t,p]$,

$$
a_{[s,t,p]}=\det_{1\leq i,j\leq s}\left(\binom{2(s+t+p)+j-2i}{s+t-j}-\binom{2(s+t+p)+j-2i}{s+t-j-2i+1}\right)
$$

and equivalently

$$
a_{[s,t,p]}=\prod_{j=1}^{s}\frac{(j-1)!(2t+2p+2j-1)!(2p+2j)_j(3t+2p+3j)_{s-j}}{(t+2p+s+2j-1)!(t+s-j)!}.
$$

The claim is attributed to Mitra et al. and uses enumerations of hexagons with cut-off corners by Ciucu and Krattenthaler. Its resolution is not stated in the supplied text."

A **nearly neighborly centrally symmetric $d$-sphere** is a centrally symmetric $d$-dimensional triangulated sphere whose faces satisfy the nearly neighborly condition, and a **vertex-transitive cyclic group action** is a cyclic group action transitive on its vertices. Let $C_d^{\Delta}$ denote the $d$-dimensional crosspolytope and let $\partial C_d^{\Delta}$ be its boundary complex.

**Centrally symmetric cyclic upper bound conjecture.** If $d$ is even, then the boundary complex $\partial C_d^{\Delta}$ of the $d$-dimensional crosspolytope on $n=2d$ vertices is the only nearly neighborly centrally symmetric $d$-sphere with a vertex-transitive cyclic group action.

This is a uniqueness assertion for the extremal case of the centrally symmetric cyclic upper bound problem. "Let $\mathfrak S\subset\mathbb Z^2$ be a finite set of steps. For walks on the slit plane starting at the origin, define the generating function counted by length and final coordinates by

$$
S(x,y;t)=\sum_{\substack{\text{$W$ walk on the slit plane}\\ \text{starting at the origin}\\ \text{with steps in $\mathfrak S$}}} t^{\operatorname{length} W}x^{\operatorname{x-final} W}y^{\operatorname{y-final} W}.
$$

Suppose that the set of steps is not degenerated, so that all four quadrants of the plane can be reached by some walk, and that the greatest common divisor of the vertical parts of the steps is equal to one. **Bousquet-Mélou's conjecture.** The generating function $S(x,y;t)$ is algebraic in $t$ if and only if the height of any step is at most one.

The claim characterizes algebraic generating functions for a broad class of slit-plane walks; the paper proves a special case, while the full assertion is presented as a conjecture."

"Let $q$ be an odd prime power, let $\beta$ be a primitive element of $\mathbb F_{q^2}$, and define

$$
C_r=\{(1,y,\beta y^2+r)\mid y\in\mathbb F_{q^2}\}\cup\{(0,0,1)\}
$$

for $r\in\mathbb F_q$. Set

$$
U_{\beta}=\bigcup_{r\in\mathbb F_q}C_r
$$

and let $\mathcal U_{\beta}$ be the $2-(q^3+1,q+1,1)$ design whose points are the points of $U_{\beta}$ and whose blocks are the intersections of secant lines with $U_{\beta}$. The **2-rank conjecture.** The binary incidence code of $\mathcal U_{\beta}$ has dimension, or equivalently the $2$-rank of $\mathcal U_{\beta}$, equal to

$$
\operatorname{dim} C_2(\mathcal U_{\beta})=q^3+1-q.
$$

The proposition preceding this conjecture gives the upper bound $\operatorname{dim} C_2(\mathcal U_{\beta})\le q^3+1-q$; the conjecture asserts that this bound is attained for these Buekenhout-Metz unital designs."

statement_token:
"Let $w$ be a special permutation with code

$$
\operatorname{code}(w)=(n,*,n-1,*,n-2,\dots,*,2,*,1,0,0,\dots),
$$

where each $*$ is either $0$ or empty. Let $a_1<\cdots<a_k=n+k$ be the positions of the zeros in the code that are preceded by a nonzero entry. Define

$$
a_\delta(y_1,\dots,y_n)=\prod_{1\leq i<j\leq n}(y_i-y_j).
$$

An $n$-element subset $J=\{j_1,\dots,j_n\}$ of $\{1,2,\dots,n+k\}$ is valid if

$$
\#(J\cap\{a_{i-1}+1,a_{i-1}+2,\dots,a_i\})=a_i-a_{i-1}-1
$$

for $1\leq i\leq k$, with $a_0=0$, and let $\varepsilon_J=(-1)^{d_J}$, where

$$
d_J=\binom{n+k+1}{2}-1-(a_1+1)-\cdots-(a_{k-1}+1)-\sum_{i\in J}i.
$$

**The conjectured formula for $\mathfrak{D}_w$.** For special $w$,

$$
\mathfrak{D}_w=C_{nk}\sum_{J=\{j_1,\dots,j_k\}}\varepsilon_J\,a_\delta(y_{n+k-j_1+1},y_{n+k-j_2+1},\dots,y_{n+k-j_k+1}),
$$

where

$$
C_{nk}=\frac{(n+1)!(n+2)!\cdots(n+k-1)!}{\binom{n+1}{2}!}
$$

and $J$ ranges over all valid subsets of $\{1,2,\dots,n+k\}$. This gives a proposed explicit value for the polynomial $\mathfrak{D}_w$ associated with a special permutation."

"Let $X$ be a fixed non-crossing matching with $n-m$ arches, and let $X\cup m$ be the matching obtained from $X$ by adding $m$ nested arches. Let $A_X(m)$ denote the number of fully packed loop configurations having $X\cup m$ as their associated matching. Associate to $X$ a Ferrers diagram $\lambda(X)$, and write $|\lambda(X)|$ for its size and $\dim(\lambda(X))$ for the dimension of the irreducible representation of the symmetric group $S_{|\lambda(X)|}$ indexed by it.

**Zuber's conjecture.** The number $A_X(m)$ is

$$
A_X(m)=\frac{1}{|X|!}P_X(m),
$$

where $P_X(m)$ is a polynomial of degree $|\lambda(X)|$ with integer coefficients, whose highest-degree coefficient is $\dim(\lambda(X))$.

This conjecture gives a precise form of the expected polynomial dependence on the number of added nested arches; the supplied text does not establish its resolution."

"Let $X$ and $Y$ be two non-crossing matchings. Place them on the circle together with $m$ nested arches between them, and denote the resulting matching by $X\cup m\cup Y$. Let $\lambda(X)$ and $\lambda(Y)$ be the associated Ferrers diagrams, with sizes $|\lambda(X)|$ and $|\lambda(Y)|$, and let $\dim(\lambda(X))$ and $\dim(\lambda(Y))$ denote the dimensions of the corresponding irreducible representations of the symmetric groups indexed by these diagrams. Let $A_{X,Y}(m)$ be the number of fully packed loop configurations having $X\cup m\cup Y$ as their associated matching.

**Zuber's conjecture.** The number $A_{X,Y}(m)$ is

$$
A_{X,Y}(m)=\frac{1}{|\lambda(X)|!\,|\lambda(Y)|!}P_{X,Y}(m),
$$

where $P_{X,Y}(m)$ is a polynomial of degree $|\lambda(X)|+|\lambda(Y)|$ with integer coefficients, whose highest-degree coefficient is $\dim(\lambda(X))\cdot\dim(\lambda(Y))$.

This conjecture generalizes Zuber's first conjecture to nested arches placed between two matchings; the supplied text does not establish its resolution."

"Let $\lambda$ and $\mu$ be partitions, and let $\lambda\cup\mu=(\nu_1,\nu_2,\nu_3,\ldots)$ be the partition obtained by rearranging all parts of $\lambda$ and $\mu$ in weakly decreasing order. Define

$$
\operatorname{sort}_1(\lambda,\mu)=(\nu_1,\nu_3,\nu_5,\ldots),\qquad \operatorname{sort}_2(\lambda,\mu)=(\nu_2,\nu_4,\nu_6,\ldots).
$$

For symmetric functions $f$ and $g$, $f\geq_s g$ means that $f-g$ is Schur nonnegative. **Fomin–Fulton–Li–Poon's conjecture.**

$$
s_{\operatorname{sort}_1(\lambda,\mu)}s_{\operatorname{sort}_2(\lambda,\mu)}\geq_s s_\lambda s_\mu.
$$

This conjecture concerns Schur positivity arising from eigenvalue and singular-value inequalities for sums of Hermitian and complex matrices. It was also studied by Bergeron and McNamara, but the source does not specify a resolution status."

"Let ${\mathcal P}$ be a tropical polytope in the generic case. For a vertex $v$ of ${\mathcal P}$, let the grid label of $v$ have shaded boxes in its columns, and let $C_i$ denote the sector associated with index $i$. A tropical halfspace has the form $v+\bigcup_{i\in A}C_i$ for a nonempty proper subset $A$ of the sector indices.

**Partition characterization.** Every minimal halfspace with respect to ${\mathcal P}$ has the form

$$
v+\bigcup_{i\in A}C_i,
$$

where $v$ is a vertex of ${\mathcal P}$ and the shaded boxes in the columns indexed by $A$ form a partition of $[r]$.

This would refine the generally redundant halfspace description of tropical polytopes by characterizing minimal halfspaces through the grid labels of their vertices. The supplied text does not give a proof or indicate whether the assertion has been resolved."
